amendments.what: three namespaces -> four; E- reserved for event-log entries
amendments.why: an id namespace whose meaning changes later makes every recording made under it silently ambiguous

amendments.what: state_coverage gained an explicit denominator; the P/B/E shorthand left over from the three-namespace draft now reads P/B/J in the arms and canary sections. The header keeps its original wording as the historical record of what was committed on 2026-08-14.
amendments.why: the namespaces were built today (tracker task G) and the metric had to be implemented. A denominator chosen while looking at results is not a pre-registration, so it is fixed now, before any v3 recording exists. The shorthand fix is clerical: the 2026-08-15 amendment already moved journey milestones from E- to J- and the arm text was not updated with it.

amendments.implementation_bug_fixed: the clean-lever check was implemented on model_recall, not f_recall as registered. model_recall moves for a second reason — dropping the state ids makes state-only must-groups unreachable, shrinking the denominator without any citation changing — so it was the wrong reading. Corrected to f_recall, which still fires.
amendments.lever_not_clean: f_recall moves 0.5306 -> 0.6939 when the state ids are removed, against a registered note saying it should be roughly unchanged. f_recall_exclusive — over the 39 must-groups no state id can satisfy — moves with it, 0.4615 -> 0.6154, so this is NOT a mixed alternation being grounded through its profile member instead of its graph one. State ids DISPLACE graph citations for claims with no other citation path. This is the enum-incentive effect f_recall_holds_independently was registered to catch, arriving in the canary rather than in the run. It is a property of the v3 configuration, not a fault in the lever, and the arm's floor is NOT moved to accommodate it.
amendments.load_state: A cold model load and a warm one produce DIFFERENT output for identical inputs: same battery, same digest, same (seed, temperature, top_p, num_predict, num_ctx), system_recall 0.5862 / state_coverage 0.5641 cold against 0.6034 / 0.5897 warm. Each state is internally exact — two warm runs matched to 4dp, and a deliberate unload reproduced the cold figures exactly — so it is a variable, not noise. Every run now warms the model first (scripts/record_narration.py), which makes bundles comparable rather than merely annotated. Comparisons WITHIN one process, which is how the canary works, were never affected.
amendments.what: two properties of the live configuration measured before recording: the model-server LOAD STATE is a hidden variable, and the strip_state_ids lever is not clean in the registered sense
amendments.why: both were found by running the canary and then failing to reproduce its baseline. Recorded here because a reader who meets them in the results would otherwise have to guess whether they were known.

arms.note: The metric that did not exist before this build. It is what the recovery arm has to be caused BY — factual_fraction rising without state ids present is the over-correction signature.
a persona that never merely feels has been schema'd out of personhood. The point of state ids is to let circumstance be grounded, not to abolish the feeling kind.
0/30 in v2; a regression here means prompt v3 reintroduced a formatting convention the schema does not use.

caveats: model_recall and system_recall are NOT comparable to v0.1 or v0.3: those graded flat sets of retrieval-derived ids, this grades authored must/may groups. The pass_bars.json bars for them were registered against the older instrument. f_recall is the graph-recall reading for v3.
State ids make up 34% of the citations in this run, and roughly 64% of the enum by construction. A rise in state citation is partly a volume effect; f_recall is what separates the two.
57% of takes are a single segment. No metric here catches degeneracy; read the raw takes before believing any of this.
reading: RECOVERY WITHOUT STATE CITATION: the tags recovered while state_coverage stayed below its floor, which means the segments were relabelled rather than grounded. This is the over-correction signature in its purest form.
